title: Allocate by the stated weight
hook: Three trays have weights 2:1:1. Does an equal split follow those weights?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Allocate a conserved volume according to stated relative weights.

misconception: An equal split satisfies every weighted allocation rule.
objective: Allocate a conserved volume according to stated relative weights.

claims.text: Three empty trays have allocation weights 2:1:1. Compare volume assigned to the first tray. Scaled model; empty trays; arithmetic allocation only.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Total=8L, A=4L and B=2.667L. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",2]; B=["/","x",3]; x denotes Total. At x=8, A=4, B=2.66666666667. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The weights add to four. The first tray receives two of four units, or half the total. Splitting into three equal shares uses a different rule and produces a different allocation.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["/","x",2]; B=["/","x",3]; x denotes Total. At x=8, A=4, B=2.66666666667. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Three empty trays have allocation weights 2:1:1, and 12L is allocated. How much goes to tray one? Correct: 6L. The weights add to four and tray one holds two of them: half of 12L is 6L. An equal split would give 4L.

recall.question: Three empty trays have allocation weights 2:1:1, and 12L is allocated. How much goes to tray one?
recall.why: The weights add to four and tray one holds two of them: half of 12L is 6L. An equal split would give 4L.
